canonical.sourceFilePath: 11. Binary Trees/2. Medium Problems/05. Same Tree.cpp

narrative.title: The Twin Chandelier Inspection
narrative.scenario: A glasswork atelier hand-builds chandeliers as binary branch trees, and a wealthy client ordered two supposedly identical pieces. Before shipping, the quality clerk hangs both on rigging and compares them joint by joint: every joint must hold the same crystal grade, and every branch must fork the same way. A single mismatched fork or swapped child disqualifies the pair.
narrative.inputFormat: Two binary trees p and q, each given as a level-order array where null marks a missing child.
narrative.outputFormat: Return true if the trees are structurally identical with matching values at every position, false otherwise.
constraints: 0 <= number of nodes in each tree <= 10^5

testCases.explanation: Same shape, same values at every joint — identical pieces.
The branch hangs left in p but right in q — a structural mismatch.

hintLevels: Level 1: Walk both trees in lockstep — the comparison is decided at the first position where they disagree.
Level 2: Handle the null algebra first: both null is a match, one null is a mismatch, both present compares values.
Level 3: Then recurse on left-with-left and right-with-right; the AND of all three checks is the answer.
